usageNotes: Use this to run a command inside a running VM via the QEMU guest agent; the VM must be powered on and have the guest agent service running (qemu-guest-agent installed and active). The call returns immediately with the spawned process PID — the command runs asynchronously inside the guest, so use get_nodes_node_qemu_vmid_agent_exec_status with the returned PID to poll for exit code and output. Requires the VM.GuestAgent.Unrestricted privilege on /vms/{vmid}; pass the command as an array (program + args) to avoid shell quoting issues.

examples.summary: Run a one-shot hostname check inside VM 101 on node pve1

tips: Pass command as an array, not a shell string — the guest agent does not invoke a shell, so redirection and pipes will not work unless you explicitly invoke the shell (e.g. ["/bin/sh", "-c", "echo hello > /tmp/out"]).
Use the 'input-data' field to send data to the process's stdin (up to 64 KiB); useful for scripting or piping payloads without writing temp files inside the guest.
The returned PID belongs to the guest OS namespace, not the hypervisor — it cannot be tracked from the Proxmox host side.
If the guest agent is not running, the API returns an error immediately; check agent status with get_nodes_node_qemu_vmid_agent_info first.
